question: For the Land Use Framework we need to compare the greenhouse-gas return per hectare of three land-use changes in East Anglia over the next 25 years: raising the water table on drained Fenland arable peat, planting new woodland on arable land in Breckland, and planting hedgerow and agroforestry trees on Fenland farms. How does each compare per hectare, and how big is livestock methane in the same area by comparison? Which should be prioritised, and how confident can we be?

assumptions.assumption: 25-year appraisal period, 2026-2050; per-hectare averages are cumulative 25-year totals divided by 25.
assumptions.rationale: Question asks for the next 25 years; it matches the 2050 net zero date.

assumptions.assumption: Baseline is winter wheat on drained Fen peat at the DT8 Fenland water-table climatology (about 0.66 m). Rewetting options are mean water tables of 0.30, 0.10 and 0.0 m with reed (paludiculture) vegetation, an established regime (3 years since rewetting), AR6 GWP100 as DT8 uses.
assumptions.rationale: Winter wheat is the main Fenland arable crop; DT8 models drained peat in the East Anglian Fens.

assumptions.assumption: New woodland on bare arable land in the Thetford landscape (stands in for Breckland), planted in 2026, no intervention, 25 years, per 100 ha; Corsican pine (dominant local conifer) and mixed broadleaves compared.
assumptions.rationale: Thetford Forest is in Breckland and is the DT4 pilot there.

assumptions.assumption: DT6 'fens' pilot tile stands in for Fenland farms. Planting of 1,000 trees per type (hedgerow, agroforestry) from 2025 for 25 years, rescaled per hectare assuming 100 agroforestry trees per ha of field and an illustrative 10 hedgerow trees per ha of farm (about 1 tree per 10 m of hedge at ~100 m hedge/ha). These densities are assumptions, not agent outputs.
assumptions.rationale: DT6 works per number of trees; a density is needed to express results per hectare.

assumptions.assumption: East Anglia Fens and Breckland approximated by the BNG box [520000, 260000, 600000, 320000] (80 km x 60 km, 480,000 ha); NAEI comparison for the same box.
assumptions.rationale: Covers the Fens around Ely, March and Wisbech and Breckland around Thetford.

assumptions.assumption: Each agent's native GWP is reported (DT8 AR6 GWP100; DT2 both AR5 and AR6). Sign: positive = emission.

Woodland mask from the NFI woodland map GB 2024; species groups, planting years (stand ages) and Forestry England yield classes from the FE sub-compartment database. FE yield class is only an independent check, never used in calibration.
Pixels outside the FE estate take a species group from the NFI forest type (conifer, felled and young types: the landscape's dominant conifer; broadleaved types: mixed broadleaves).
3-PG climate: HadUK-Grid 1991-2020 monthly averages (Met Office portal, ~2 km and 12 km grids); radiation estimated from the diurnal temperature range (Hargreaves-Samani).
CCI v7 saturates at about 150 Mg/ha in these forests; calibration compares CCI with min(model AGB, 150). Each pixel is treated as an unthinned even-aged stand.

assumptions: Inventory: National Trees Outside Woodland map V1 (lone trees, groups of trees, small woodlands; canopy > 3 m outside NFI woodland). NFI overhanging canopy is left to DT4, hedges below 3 m to DT5.
Calibrated on Environment Agency lidar canopy heights only: first and last return of the National LIDAR Programme and last-return LIDAR Tiles DSMs back to 1998, all above the NLP terrain model.
Biomass from crown size and height with Jucker et al. (2017); trees in groups share the object's crown area equally; leaf type is a pilot prior (no open leaf-type map for TOW).
Crown light-use model climate: HadUK-Grid 1991-2020 monthly averages; radiation from Hargreaves-Samani.
Trees removed before the TOW map was made (2016-2023 lidar) are not in the inventory, so their loss is not seen.

result.method: Latest lidar epoch held out; each object fitted on its earlier epochs with the pilot prior learned from the other half of the objects (two-fold); forecast of the last-return height at the latest flight compared with persistence (no growth since the previous epoch). Shipped results from scripts/calibrate_pilots.py.

1.caption: Avoided emissions plus removals, t CO2e per ha over 25 years (positive = benefit), relative to drained winter wheat on Fen peat for rewetting [R1, R2, R12], and to bare arable for woodland [R3, R4] and Fenland tree planting [R5, R6]. The two series are the two growth models (rewetting has one model, so both bars are the same). Tree-planting values are rescaled from 1,000 trees at assumed densities of 100 agroforestry trees/ha and 10 hedgerow trees/ha.

2.caption: DT8 water-table scenario with reed vegetation (CO2, CH4) and the winter-wheat N2O regime, t CO2e/ha/yr, AR6 GWP100 [R2]. The drained winter-wheat baseline is 37.3 t CO2e/ha/yr at 0.66 m [R1].
